$comment: Single source of truth for vendor SDK pinning. Consumed by:
- build/VendorPinsGenerator - emits pwiz/src/Vendor/Common/VendorSdkPins.generated.cs
(the runtime resolver's pin table)
- installer/build.ps1 - flattens 'prefixes' into the staging filter that strips
vendor DLLs out of the MSI
Paths are repo-relative. Most archives live under pwiz_aux/msrc/utility/; Thermo on the
pwiz-sharp side has its own newer .NET-8-compatible copy under pwiz-sharp/vendor-archives/.

vendors.name: Bruker
$comment: TDF / TSF / BAF only. The CompassXtract stack that YEP and FID need is split into the
BrukerCompassXtract archive below, so the common case does not download 3 MB of
2008-era COM binaries it will never load. That split is why this points at a pwiz-sharp
copy instead of pwiz_aux/msrc/utility/vendor_api_Bruker.7z: the upstream archive is
shared with the C++ build, which still wants CompassXtract in the same archive.

vendors.name: BrukerCompassXtract
$comment: Bruker's legacy CompassXtract COM server: needed only for YEP (Esquire / HCT ion trap)
and FID (flex MALDI) data. Nothing in it is bound as a managed assembly or through
DllImport - the reader activates EDAL.MSAnalysis as a registration-free COM class - so
neither of VendorSdkLoader's resolvers fires for it. These prefixes exist for the
installer's MSI staging filter; pwiz/src/Vendor/Bruker/CompassXtractActivationContext.cs
calls VendorSdkLoader.EnsureExtracted("BrukerCompassXtract") explicitly, then builds a
CreateActCtx activation context from the extracted Interop.EDAL.SxS.manifest.
Interop.EDAL.dll / Interop.HSREADWRITELib.dll are deliberately absent: under
EmbedInteropTypes they are build-time inputs only. HSReadWrite.dll and its SxS manifest
ARE required even though no code calls them - Interop.EDAL.SxS.manifest declares a
dependency on Interop.HSREADWRITELib.SxS, and the process will not start without it.
The VC90 CRT / MFC / OpenMP runtime these binaries link against is not here either:
vendored in pwiz_tools/Shared/Lib/Microsoft.VC90.{CRT,MFC}/x64, staged app-local as
per-assembly folders by Bruker.csproj, and mirrored into this cache directory by
CompassXtractActivationContext.StageVc90Runtime so the activation context's own
assembly directory can satisfy them privately.

vendors.name: Bruker-linux
$comment: Bruker is the one vendor whose Windows and Linux native libraries live in separate
archives (see Bruker.csproj: one archive per OS so nobody downloads binaries for a
platform they are not building for). Both answer to the same prefixes, so 'os' narrows
the match - without it Linux would fetch the 10.7 MB Windows archive and still not find
libtimsdata.so. Waters needs no equivalent: its single archive carries both platforms.
